title: MEXT Scholarship for 2027 - Embassy Recommendation (Research Students)
funding: Fully funded government scholarship (tuition + stipend + airfare + insurance)
official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan
program_type: Government scholarship (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology)
duration: 1-2 years (Research Student non-regular phase); standard period of intended Master's/Ph.D. course thereafter. Total up to 5 years. Scholarship period ends March 2029 for 2027 intake.
description: The MEXT Scholarship Embassy Recommendation for Research Students is the Japanese government scholarship route in which candidates apply through their national Japanese embassy or consulate general, which conducts the first screening, and are then selected by MEXT to undertake research at a Japanese host institution. For the 2027 cycle, recruitment of students arriving in April 2027 or September/October 2027 is conducted between April and May of the previous year, with first screening by the embassies between May and July. title: ANRF Ramanujan Fellowship
description: The Ramanujan Fellowship, operated by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, is a reverse brain drain scheme that brings brilliant Indian and Indian-origin scientists and engineers from abroad to take up scientific research positions in India. It is scientist-specific and highly selective, restricted to candidates below 40 years of age who hold a higher degree such as a PhD in science or engineering, a master's in engineering or technology, or an MD, with adequate professional experience and a proven track record evidenced by publications and recognition. title: Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme
program_type: Government-funded postgraduate research scholarship, bottom-up researcher-initiated
description: The Government of Ireland Postgraduate Scholarship Programme awards individual, prestigious research scholarships to excellent postgraduate researchers in Ireland. Research Ireland runs the programme, funded by the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science. The award is worth up to €34,000 per annum for 1-4 years, made up of a €25,000 stipend, a fee contribution of up to €5,750 and €3,250 of eligible direct costs. Applications are assessed by international independent expert peer review.

title: Ireland Fellows Programme
official_source: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Irish Aid), Government of Ireland
duration: One year (10-16 months depending on the programme)
description: The Ireland Fellows Programme offers people from around the world the opportunity to spend one year studying at Master's level in Ireland. It is fully funded by the Irish Government and offered under the auspices of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and is managed by the Embassy of Ireland responsible for each applicant's eligible country. The award covers programme fees, flights, accommodation and living costs for a one-year Master's placement running 10 to 16 months. title: Hardiman PhD Scholarships
description: The Hardiman PhD Scholarships are University of Galway's flagship doctoral scholarships, fully funded for four years with a stipend of €25,000 per annum plus tuition fee cover, for students starting a full-time structured PhD on 1 September. Applicants must nominate one supervisor, submit a complete application, and have two academic reference forms filed by referees, all by the stated February deadline. The application system normally re-opens in early December for the following September intake, and the number of awards varies annually with available funding.

title: DCU International Scholarships for Non-EU Students
program_type: This merit based scholarship is available for high achieving Non-EU applicants that have received an offer to study on a postgraduate programme in the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences.
description: Dublin City University offers partial merit-based international scholarships to non-EU students across its four faculties and the DCU Business School. Applicants are automatically considered when they apply as a non-EU student, and only successful recipients are notified by email, with the reduction applied directly to their student account. The value varies by faculty and programme, ranging from €1,850 to €6,100 off the full-time 2027-28 Non-EU tuition fee. Recipients cannot also be considered for another DCU scholarship.

title: Government of Ireland Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme
description: The Government of Ireland Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme supports suitably qualified applicants to pursue a postdoctoral fellowship at an eligible higher education institution in Ireland for one or two years. Research Ireland manages the programme on behalf of the Department of Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science. The 2026 offer is a salary of €47,273 in year one rising to €47,880 in year two, plus the employer's PRSI contribution and €5,000 per annum of eligible direct research expenses. Selection is by international, independent expert peer review.
